note: Stage A — answers produced without reading data/questions/** answers, explanations, or content-cards. Sourced only from reviews/blind/M.json plus domain knowledge (Sanger/Chan/Rabenseifner AllReduce cost model; GSPMD paper; DDP/NCCL semantics; GPipe pipeline bubble).

answers.reasoning: All-to-All is the collective in which every rank sends a distinct per-destination shard and receives per-source shards, with no reduction. This exactly matches MoE dispatch/combine semantics (each rank routes tokens to the rank holding the target expert).

AllReduce(sum) leaves every rank with a tensor of shape S equal to Σᵢ Tᵢ. AllGather leaves every rank with shape [N,*S] stacked. A is wrong (no automatic 1/N scaling for sum-AllReduce). C reverses the two. D is factually wrong.

A: compiler inserts collectives, runtime chooses algorithm — correct SPMD/NCCL boundary. B: algorithm/chunk/lane are runtime concerns, opaque at StableHLO — correct. C: fault tolerance is runtime/framework — correct. D: compiler does not need topology to emit correct IR; topology awareness affects performance heuristics, not correctness — false.

Bucketing amortizes α (latency term) across many small tensors; trade-off is the launch is delayed until the last gradient in the bucket is produced, reducing overlap window with backward. A/B/C misstate NCCL semantics or gradient math.
Ring-AllReduce = ring-ReduceScatter (~(N-1)/N · S) + ring-AllGather (~(N-1)/N · S) = 2·(N-1)/N · S / BW per-rank bandwidth term. Standard Chan/Rabenseifner result.

A: AR = RS + AG, so 2·(N-1)/N · S — correct. B: false, ring-AG per rank is (N-1)/N · S, not N·S (each rank sends its shard around the ring). C: correct ring-AG cost. D: RS per rank is (N-1)/N · S, matching AG — correct.

T(1KB) = 10μs + 100ps × 1024 ≈ 10μs + 0.1μs ≈ 10μs (latency dominated). T(10MB) = 10μs + 100ps × 10⁷ = 10μs + 1ms ≈ 1ms (bandwidth dominated). Increasing 1KB→10KB adds ~1μs, negligible vs 10μs. A/B/D miscompute units.

GSPMD propagation pushes user annotations through op-specific sharding rules and inserts reshard collectives at boundaries where producer and consumer sharding disagree. A (runtime autotuner), B (P2P-only), and C (bypass XLA/direct CUDA) are all wrong about GSPMD's design.

The GSPMD paper explicitly states annotations are 'hints' precisely because the user does not annotate every tensor — the compiler propagates and inserts reshards. B (runtime per-step), C (drops annotations), D (strict error) all mischaracterize the paper's stance.

Device Mesh is a logical named-axis grid; runtime is free to map mesh coords to physical devices (e.g., align an axis with NVLink domain). B (exclusive to one axis) is false — 2D sharding is fundamental. C (physical) contradicts the abstraction. D (no IR representation) is false — mesh is represented in HLO/StableHLO sharding attributes.

Overlap requires (i) collective on a distinct non-blocking stream from backward compute (B) and (ii) no consumer dependency until a later sync point (C). A is false — GPUs achieve overlap via streams, no dedicated comm core needed. D would eliminate overlap by serializing.

Classic GPipe bubble fraction is (P-1)/(P+M-1); increases M shrinks the fraction, at the cost of holding activations for more in-flight microbatches (or paying recomputation). A/C/D misstate the geometry.

ReduceScatter reduces elementwise and scatters — each rank keeps a disjoint 1/N shard. Composition identity: AllReduce = ReduceScatter + AllGather. A (rank-0-only) is Reduce, not RS. B (alias of A2A) is false. C reverses the composition.

C: sharded→replicated = AllGather along the mesh axis (correct). D: partial-sum→replicated = AllReduce (correct — the classic reshard for matmul contracting axis). A is wrong (D0→D1 requires an All-to-All-like reshard, not just local reshape). B is wrong (replicated→sharded is a local slice, no AllReduce).

B: manual/MPMD requires per-rank code + explicit collectives — correct. C: SPMD partitioning rewrites a single-device-semantics program into a per-rank program with reshard collectives at boundaries — correct. D: annotations propagate — correct. A is false — sharding attributes DO cause per-rank differences within an SPMD program (each rank owns a shard); the constraint is that the *program* is single, not that per-rank data is identical.
